Scenario 3 — Be your teammate's moving cover
Warrior/Hunter (Team A) versus Rogue (Team B)

THE CHALLENGE
Team A has Warrior at 81 HP and Hunter at 1 HP; Team B has Rogue at 100 HP. HP means remaining health. Scores are tied 19–19, with 20 needed to win. Ten ticks remain, from step 290 to 300, on the approved six-wall battlefield. Waves occur every five ticks: if the match continues, initially dead slots revive after tick 5 and can make decisions from tick 6. This is not a three-agent-only fight for the entire horizon. The next decisive kill can end the match. Use terminal Team A reward: +1 SUCCESS, 0 DRAW, −1 FAIL. A simultaneous 20–20 finish is a draw; a win on step 300 still counts.

THE FEW RULES YOU NEED
A tick is one simultaneous decision. Each agent chooses movement and a Basic attack, an Ultimate special ability, or no combat before resolution. The three initially living agents start with Ultimate cooldown 11, so their Ultimates remain unavailable during all ten decisions. Hunter attacks from range and its Basic briefly slows the target. Warrior fights up close. Kiting means attacking while moving to keep an enemy from reaching you.

Agents are physical discs of radius 0.5. They cannot simply pass through one another, and collision resolution may displace a unit that chose Stay. A body obstructs movement, not sight; standing behind Warrior does not automatically make Hunter untargetable. Warrior's nearby damage-mitigation aura is a separate effect, not the physical screen. Submitted movement is an intention; walls and other bodies determine the actual endpoint.

THE PURSUER
Choose SharedObs and Reactive TDM BETA for Team B. SharedObs supplies authorized current teammate sightings, not hidden intentions or future actions. BETA hunts observed living enemy Priests first, Mages second and Hunters third. Initially only Warrior and Hunter are alive on Team A, so Rogue pursues Hunter even if Warrior becomes weaker. If revived Priests or Mages enter shared sight later, that priority can change its destination.

Prey sets Rogue's destination; legal targets and health set its attack. It can attack Warrior while chasing Hunter. Its route estimate allows glancing shoulder contact and treats observed bodies as stationary. It cannot read Team A's pending moves, so a moving Warrior can block its chosen route.

THE COORDINATED POSITIONING IDEA
Keep Warrior between Rogue and Hunter, adjusting to the likely approach while both defenders continue attacking. An imaginary line from Rogue toward Hunter passing through Warrior's body is a useful starting picture. It is a positioning guide, not a guaranteed or universally optimal block: the Rogue can angle around a shoulder, and everyone's movement resolves together.

Both teammates maintain the screen. Warrior covers Rogue's likely lane; Hunter moves around Warrior's protected side. Leave each other room to move and avoid trapping Hunter against walls. Warrior is a moving pillar, not a stationary shield.

Protection alone is insufficient. Warrior attacks when legally in reach, and Hunter keeps ranged damage flowing while repositioning. Chasing damage can expose the 1-HP Hunter, but simply fleeing can run out the clock. The verified sequence below shows one way to apply these principles.

ONE VERIFIED WINNING SEQUENCE — 2026-09-15
Use SharedObs, Manual Team A and BETA Team B. Hunter is listed first. Both Hunter and Warrior Basic-attack Rogue-B whenever their current legal-action masks allow it; otherwise choose no combat. Use no Ultimates. Other Team A agents Stay with no combat, including after respawn. Team B chooses fresh actions each turn.

Turn | Hunter | Warrior
1 | North | North
2 | North | Southeast
3 | South | East
4 | South | South
5 | North | North
6 | North | South
7 | North | North
8 | East | Southwest

Team A wins 20–19 at step 298. Warrior finishes at 9.6 HP and Hunter at 1 HP. Both attack Rogue on turns 1–7; Warrior takes 10.2 damage each turn. After turn 7's North/North move, Hunter can still attack on turn 8 but Warrior and Rogue cannot Basic each other. Hunter finishes the 2-HP Rogue while Warrior stays at 9.6 HP.

One matched alternative removes turn 4's South/South, shifts the remaining commands earlier and adds Stay/Stay at the end, with legal Basics. The first three turns match, but Hunter dies on turn 7: Team A loses 19–20, with Warrior at 30 HP and Rogue at 10 HP. The match ends before the extra Stay/Stay command. This shows why the omitted move matters in this continuation; it does not prove all other routes fail or that South/South directly creates a safe next-turn shot.

WHAT THIS SCENARIO IS DESIGNED TO TEST
- Teammate Modeling: anticipate where the partner needs protection, movement space and attack access.
- Opponent Modeling: anticipate the Hunter-pursuing Rogue's shoulder approach without observing its selected action.
- Tactical Positioning (Kiting and Body Blocking): coordinate all three bodies' likely geometry, rather than optimize each defender's position independently.
- Balancing Defensive and Offensive Play: preserve Hunter while dealing enough damage to finish before time expires.

DAMAGE PRESSURE AND EVIDENCE
For the initial pair alone, Warrior Basic deals 8 and Hunter Basic 6: seven full-output ticks supply at most 98 damage against Rogue's 100 HP. The verified route supplies those 98 damage over turns 1–7, then Hunter finishes the remaining 2 HP on turn 8. Revived agents can move from tick 6, but their Spawn Shield blocks combat and aura participation through ticks 6–8. From tick 9 they may fight or support if their exact masks, range and sight allow it; do not treat the entire horizon as an isolated three-agent duel.

The author previously reported wins at steps 298, 299 and 300 against the retired standalone Scenario 3 controller. Those remain historical observations. The author reviewed and accepted r24. That approval completed the scenario-design gate. The revised BETA v4 winning sequence above was verified separately on 2026-09-15. The older 2026-09-12 route had a different safe-shot turn and its omission drew; those results do not describe this route. A separate, older r9 test layout verifies three-tick pursuit around stationary or moving defenders; it does not establish a solution here.

Development limitation: the central room is sealed from the outside spawn pads; this already existed in r20, before the latest decorations. An ordinary entry route has not been established. This accepted diagnostic starts from the authored snapshot. Numerical consistency is not proof of full-state reachability from an ordinary reset; no additional reachability or design-approval gate is required for this approved scenario.

This scenario is intended for matched behavioral ablations under frozen conditions, not universal proof of a policy's internal reasoning or an Elo score. Official evaluation material must not guide training, tuning or checkpoint selection.

HOW TO PLAY
Load the saved scenario, keep Team A Manual, choose SharedObs and select BETA for Team B. Loading never selects a controller automatically. Reset repeats the loaded snapshot. Revived agents can make decisions from tick 6, subject to masks and Spawn Shield.

Physical setup: scenario_3 r25 preserves accepted r24. These Notes add the verified route. Ten transitions test sustained body blocking; five-tick waves remain canonical. This is the sole horizon exception among the eight approved scenarios. BETA is internally scenario_5 v4. With no observed living Priest, Mage or Hunter, Rogue moves toward ALPHA's nearest observed enemy, otherwise map center. Its Basic-radius combat rule remains; non-Rogues use ALPHA.
